title: Tom Anderson's mouthpiece trick and tips
summary: Correcting his pay at Anderson's to $25 and tips from actors; mention of a different Louis.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Getting paid: wages, scale and the pay envelope

blocks.x: 1933. Well, you mentioned too that you made a mistake when you told about him playing on the mouthpiece at Tom Anderson's. Oh, yeah, yeah, Tom.

I said it was $10, and Mama said it's $25. $25. And she said in those days they had what they called the kitty. Mm-hmm. And they told him... That wasn't for the kitty, that was for him. That was for him especially. That was for him especially. That's why people put the tips at him.
Yeah. That's what they used to call it. But they gave him the $25 just for playing that. Yes.
On that mouthpiece. And he also used to get tips for himself when he'd get through playing and the actors would come in at Anderson and he'd play for them to sing and they'd tip him to play.
I believe Professor Mineta was who told us how he played at the old tuxedo dance hall too. Oh, yes. Fantastic. That was with Louis Keough. That was the uncle I guess of your teacher. That's poor.
Well, that's the one you all want to interview. No, this is a different Louis.
Oh, it's been a young... Oh, yeah. Oh, yeah. This is a young...
